meaning: The library index's list of papers, in the order the page shows them. An entry with "library": true is a paper built here from instances/<id>/; its title, authors, credit and pages come from its instance.json and its counts from its published edition, so the entry adds only the sentence. Every other entry is a paper still on its current site: its title, authors, sentence and pages are taken from that site's own front matter (proof-reader papers/*/paper.toml and links.json, the lean-exposition examples, quartic-query-lean's README and site), and its counts were read from the files named in counted_from. Credit lines here never name Anthropic; the full credit is on each paper's own page.

papers.sentence: Constructs smooth periodic initial data for the three-dimensional incompressible Euler equations whose solution blows up in finite time, with the velocity bounded and the vorticity at the origin tending to infinity.

Proves that there are smooth, compactly supported, divergence-free initial data on ℝ³, and smooth divergence-free data on the torus, whose solutions of the unforced three-dimensional Navier–Stokes equations blow up in finite time, with the profile obtained from a numerical certificate the authors will release.

Proves that the sum of 1/(2ᵃ − 1) over an infinite set A is irrational when A satisfies a weighted summability condition, has a summable divisor cover, or lies in a union of one set of each kind, at every integer base b ≥ 2; Erdős’s question for every infinite A stays open.
papers.comparator: Comparator accepted all 51 statements replayed on GitHub Actions.

papers.sentence: A minimising Parisi order parameter of the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick spin glass has no gaps: it increases across every interval in [0, 1), and its derivative is positive between 0 and 1.

For every power below four there is a total Boolean function whose randomized query complexity exceeds that power of its quantum query complexity, and four is the best possible exponent. Three accounts of OpenAI’s proof, each linked phrase by phrase to the Lean, which checks the optimal exponent with no hypothesis.

pages.title: OpenAI’s paper and the verification details, in the old reader’s last edition

papers.title: Constant-query verification by algebraic encoding
authors: Will Cook, with AI assistance (explanatory reconstruction)
papers.sentence: The PCP theorem: every language in NP has a polynomial-time verifier with logarithmic randomness, constantly many proof-bit queries, perfect completeness and soundness error at most one half, by the algebraic proof of Amireddy, Behera, Srinivasan, Sudan and Willumsgaard.
papers.credit: Original algebraic proof by Amireddy, Behera, Srinivasan, Sudan and Willumsgaard. Lean formalization by Troy Lee.
papers.where: On its current site, Proof Reader.
papers.comparator: Comparator accepted the forward theorem, its converse and the equivalence with the reference NP class.

pages.title: Checking a long proof by reading a few bits

papers.title: Contextual Embeddings: Implementing Bound Variables Through Instance Resolution
papers.sentence: Uses instance resolution to define a context-directed isomorphism between a higher-order interface for bound variables and a first-order representation, and proves the round trip in Lean.
papers.credit: Paper and Lean by the authors, from their PLDI 2026 artifact, under CC BY 4.0.
papers.where: On its current site, Proof Reader.

papers.title: The SMT-LIB Standard: Version 2.7
papers.sentence: The reference standard for SMT-LIB 2.7, read beside BSmtLib, a Lean formalisation of its lexicon, grammar and parser.
papers.credit: BSmtLib by Jan Onderka, Armin Biere and Henrik Böving.
papers.where: On its current site, Proof Reader.

papers.title: The minimum of the coupled spring potential
authors: AI agents under Will Cook’s direction (the page)
papers.sentence: The coupled spring potential U(x₀, x₁) = x₀² + x₀x₁ + x₁² has a local minimum at the origin, proved in PhyslibAlpha by a general second-derivative test.
papers.credit: Lean formalization by Bjørn Kjos-Hanssen, PhyslibAlpha in Physlib at be0a9ee.
papers.where: On its current site, Proof Reader.
papers.comparator: Comparator accepted the local-minimum theorem and rejected a control that asked for a local maximum.

papers.title: Gauge theory: Physlib’s API map
papers.sentence: Physlib’s own map of its gauge theory formalisation, read beside the Lean files it cites.
papers.credit: API map and Lean by the Physlib contributors, at be0a9ee.
papers.where: On its current site, Proof Reader.
